title: Slide a monitor out from under a desk shelf to fit a clip-on light bar, then slide it back
instruction: Fit the light bar on top of the monitor and leave the monitor where it started.
context: Fitting accessories to desk equipment is routine office IT work. The monitor stands pushed back under a desk shelf with 4 cm above its top edge. Not stated: the light bar's clip has a counterweight that hangs 6.5 cm behind the screen, so it cannot be lowered onto the edge there; this shows only when the clip meets the shelf. The monitor must be slid out, the bar hung on it, and the monitor slid back; the fitted bar adds only 2.8 cm and passes under. Unlike leaning a tall canister in under a low shelf, where the part is tilted through the gap, here the part cannot pass, so the host object is moved out and put back within 2 cm. Unlike moving a lamp closer before pulling its plug, the moved object must go back carrying the fitted part. Unlike unlocking and rotating a monitor to portrait, which tests finding which unmarked button releases which spring-locked axis and positioning the screen, here the monitor is only a workpiece moved out of an obstruction and returned.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Desk shelf, free-standing, pine, 4.6 kg: a board 120 x 25 x 1.8 cm on two end panels 25 x 1.8 x 42.4 cm, so the board's underside is 42.4 cm above the desk; front edge at x 36, back edge at x 61, centred on y 0. Monitor, 21.5-inch on its fixed stand (as the Dell SE2222H), black plastic, 2.67 kg in all: screen panel 50.4 wide x 29.5 tall x 1.6 cm thick at its edges, bottom edge 8.9 cm and top edge 38.4 cm above the desk; rear housing 30 x 20 x 3.3 cm behind the middle of the panel; stand neck behind it; stand base 17.9 deep x 18 wide x 1.5 cm reaching 5 cm in front of the screen. It stands pushed back under the shelf: screen front face at x 42 (6 cm behind the shelf's front edge), centred on y 0, facing the robot, 4 cm between the top edge of the screen and the shelf. Light bar (as the BenQ ScreenBar), 0.53 kg: an aluminium bar 45 cm long and 2.2 cm across (0.25 kg) fixed along the front of a dark clip 4.5 cm wide (0.28 kg with its counterweight). The clip is a top plate 7.5 x 4.5 x 0.6 cm, a front lip hanging 1.2 cm down in front of the screen, and a counterweight block 3 x 4.5 x 6.5 cm hanging behind the screen, 2.1 cm from the lip. Fitted, the bar's axis is 2 cm in front of and 1.7 cm above the screen's top edge and its top 2.8 cm above the edge; the centre of mass of the whole bar is over the edge, 9 mm behind the screen's face. The bar lies on its back on the desk in front of the monitor: the counterweight's back face flat on the desk, the clip pointing toward the robot, the bar's axis 7 cm above the desk along y at x 14, clip at y 0. Friction coefficients: monitor 0.5, shelf 0.5, light bar 0.6.
scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler, a protractor and photos from the front and the side. 0 if at any time the monitor tipped more than 20 degrees from upright or the shelf moved more than 1 cm from its start. Otherwise 1.0 if the light bar sits on the monitor's top edge: the clip's top plate resting on the edge (its underside from 3 mm below to 6 mm above the edge), the front lip in front of the screen (its inside within 7 mm of the screen's front face) and the counterweight behind it, the middle of the clip within 3 cm of the middle of the edge, the bar running along the edge (within about 25 degrees), the bar level within 5 degrees and the clip upright within 15 degrees; the monitor is back within 2 cm of its start position and turned less than 5 degrees; every finger of both grippers is at least 3 cm from the light bar and 2 cm from the monitor; and over the last second (1 s) neither the bar nor the monitor moved more than 1 mm and both grippers stayed clear of them. 0.5 if the bar sits on the edge in the same way, let go and still, but the monitor is not back within 2 cm and 5 degrees of its start (for example left pulled out). Otherwise 0, including a bar left on the desk, dropped, or resting on the edge on its lip.
reset_notes: Lift the light bar off the monitor and lay it on its back (counterweight face down, bar up) on its marked outline; slide the monitor back into its marked outline under the shelf; set the shelf in its marked outline.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and one cylinder at real size and mass (monitor 50.4 x 38.4 cm, 2.67 kg; bar 45 cm, 0.53 kg). The monitor's tilt hinge is not modelled: the screen is fixed upright. The clip is a rigid U with a fixed 2.1 cm opening around the 1.6 cm edge and no spring, so the fitted bar is held by gravity and its counterweight behind the screen, not by a clamping force; its centre of mass is set 9 mm behind the screen's face. The shelf is free and moves if struck.
